questions.stem_text:
Analysis of the teeth of a hominid species discovered in Malapa Cave in South Africa,
dating just after 2 million years ago, indicates a diet that consisted primarily of:

options.B: primarily C3 plants that included barley and oats.
options.C: large quantities of insects and small mammals.
options.D: a balanced diet of fruits, vegetables, meat, and fish.
options.E: primarily C4 plants that included corn and potatoes.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - meat, fish, and some plants.

questions.stem_text: Which of the following is NOT an innovation of the Mesolithic?

options.C: European use of bow and arrow

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - crop irrigation systems

questions.stem_text: How did Aurignacian technology differ from Mousterian technology?

options.A: Mousterian technology was focused on the production of scrapers.
options.B: Aurignacian technology was primarily used for creating stone tools.
options.C: Aurignacian technology was less advanced than Mousterian technology.
options.D: Mousterian technology produced more usable blade surface.
options.E: Aurignacian technology produced more usable blade surface.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: E - Aurignacian technology produced more usable blade surface.

questions.stem_text:
In primates, the location of which of the following determines if it is a quadruped or
biped?
questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - the foramen magnum

questions.stem_text:
Research on C3 and C4 pathways indicates that changes in plant communities were associated
with a transition in the diets of ancient hominids from:

options.B: species focused on grasses to fruits and vegetables.
options.D: nuts and fruits to species more focused on grasses.
options.E: species focused on grasses to meat.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - nuts and fruits to species more focused on grasses.
